I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsbwtg.title: Provider selection is not applied to the Lithos Responses route
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUsbwtg.body:
## What is wrong

`handleResponsesInternal` dispatches an explicit Lithos id to `handleLithosResponses` with no provider-selection check (`src/responses-handler.ts:794-796`), while the adjacent DeepSeek, Cerebras and OpenRouter branches all test `isProviderEnabled(<provider>, await loadProviderSelectionCached())` (`:788-789`, `:801-802`, `:807-808`). With a configured Lithos key and a saved selection that excludes `lithos`, an explicit Lithos `/v1/responses` request still reaches the paid upstream — the route ignores the operator's switch entirely.

## Where

- Repository: `ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi`
- Validated against: `5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b` (`development`)
- Location: `src/responses-handler.ts:794-796` (Lithos branch without a selection check) versus `:788-789` (DeepSeek), `:801-802` (Cerebras) and `:807-808` (OpenRouter), which call `isProviderEnabled`
- `src/provider/lithos-handlers.ts` contains no `isProviderEnabled` use, so the branch itself never rechecks
- Links: [Lithos branch](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b/src/responses-handler.ts#L794-L796), [DeepSeek branch](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b/src/responses-handler.ts#L788-L789), [Cerebras branch](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b/src/responses-handler.ts#L801-L802), [OpenRouter branch](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/blob/5c58eca89b88d7e4004521ece5350e5bebb76c1b/src/responses-handler.ts#L807-L808)

## Trigger

Disable `lithos` in the provider selection, then send `POST /v1/responses` naming a Lithos model id: the request is dispatched instead of refused.

## Acceptance

Apply the same `isProviderEnabled("lithos", ...)` gate the adjacent branches use before taking the Lithos branch, leaving the disabled id to the ordinary availability check; a focused test covers the disabled-provider case.

## Validation

Static source read at `5c58eca8` (`development`); no test, browser, inference, or production action was executed. Source PR: [ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi#443](https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/443) (merged).

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnqtkQ.title: The chat probe only recognizes localhost and 127.0.0.1
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnqtkQ.body:
## Confirmed defect

The probe is gated by isLocalDevelopmentOrigin(), which returns true only for hostname localhost or 127.0.0.1 over http (static/auth.js:17-22). A supported listener such as --host ::1 is never probed from http://[::1]:8000, and the server-side check (src/auth/index.ts:194) does accept ::1 and [::1], so the page reports "Missing token" while the server would grant the loopback bypass. Other 127/8 addresses fail identically.

## Where

- Repository: `ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi`
- Validated against: `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded`
- Location: `src/../static/chat.js:449 + src/../static/auth.js:17-22`
- Source PR: #330 (closed, merged=true), original head `682a8d0326943b4e5dc211d5b2971aa5d6279f95`, merge `e1018b7a49169128801da293d1198ddc876370c1`

## Original review finding

P2 `The chat probe only recognizes localhost and 127.0.0.1` - reported against `static/chat.js:449` by native review turn `01a0fc9d-9c7b-73b2-b2ce-01a080634137` (thread `01a0fc9d-902a-7f10-8903-bf36a99584fb`) for PR #330.

## Trigger / reproduction

Static source read at `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded` shows the cited code path unchanged; the exact expression is named above. No runtime, browser, or production operation was performed to confirm this.

## Acceptance

The client probe must recognize the loopback hosts the server accepts (::1 and [::1], and the wider 127/8 range), so a supported listener does not report "Missing token" while the server would grant the bypass. Add a focused test for ::1.

## Evidence and duplicate check

- Reviewer head `98ccd167cca1db4309e2d7f4d961b7109b119502`; validated against `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded` (source-only static read).

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnqqdQ.body:

The token input handler's empty-token branch starts the local-auth probe at static/chat.js:596 but never cancels a previously scheduled scheduleAuthCheck() debounce (scheduled at :602 for non-empty input). When that stale checkAuthToken runs it takes the empty-token branch at :397-402, resetting the model catalog and selection and showing "Missing token" even though local authentication succeeded.

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnofuA.title: Revalidation feeds the enriched body back in, so a corrected window can never decrease
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnofuA.body:
## Confirmed defect

revalidateCachedCatalog re-stores body: cached.body (index.ts:288) with the old upstream etag. cached.body is the already-widened stored body, and widenCodexModelWindows (store.ts:196-215) reads record.context_window / record.max_context_window as the endpoint's own declaration. A later narrower OpenRouter value therefore fails the widest > endpointWindow test, so the stale ceiling persists; each upstream 304 renews retention (store.ts:256 expireIn).

## Where

- Repository: `ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi`
- Validated against: `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded`
- Location: `src/catalog/store.ts:190-215 + src/catalog/index.ts:285-292`
- Source PR: #335 (closed, merged=true), original head `37396c12786e639e1de514de01ff87162e508242`, merge `adaa36f5540a9df9e07c962057d261535cfda698`

Static source read at `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded` shows the cited code path unchanged; the exact expression is named above. No runtime, browser, or production operation was performed to confirm this.

## Acceptance

I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnL0vw.title: Gate the DeepSeek thinking extension on the enabled provider route
I_kwDOQoe6nc8AAAABUnL0vw.body:
The Chat Completions envelope accepts the DeepSeek `thinking` extension based on the model id alone, while dispatch decides on the enabled provider route. A request can therefore be accepted with `thinking` and then answered by the Codex/paid bridge, which drops it.

## What is wrong
- `src/chat/envelope.ts:115`: `isDeepSeekRoute = deepSeekUpstreamModelFor(model) !== null` widens the OpenAI-schema allowlist with `DEEPSEEK_CHAT_EXTENSION_KEYS`; there is no provider-selection check.
- `src/chat/envelope.ts:566-574`: DeepSeek dispatch requires `isProviderEnabled("deepseek", selection)`; otherwise the same body continues into the ordinary Codex/paid path, where `thinking` is not forwarded and is reported as `thinking_ignored`.
- With the direct DeepSeek provider disabled and an official DeepSeek model available in the paid catalog, the caller's thinking switch is accepted without being applied on a route documented as retaining the strict OpenAI schema (`AGENTS.md:21-22`).

## Trigger
Disable the DeepSeek provider selection, send `model` naming a DeepSeek id with `thinking: {"type":"enabled"}` on `/v1/chat/completions`: the request succeeds without thinking.

## Acceptance
- The extension is admitted only when the request will actually dispatch to the enabled DeepSeek route, or it is rejected before the ordinary bridge with an actionable message.
- A focused test covers the disabled-provider case for the same model id.

## Duplicate search
- Local index (`thinking_ignored`, envelope/allowlist keys) — #580 and #579 only (stream tool-call closure; OpenRouter cold refresh); no issue for this gate.
- Fresh GitHub search, 2026-10-02: `repo:ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi is:issue "thinking ignored"` → 0.
- Current upstream rechecked: `1d7e64e6b30cef212bca16ca7191f13685382ded` (`development`); `src/chat/envelope.ts` is byte-identical to the reviewed snapshot.

## Provenance
- Source pull request: https://github.com/ubiquity/ai.ubq.fi/pull/391 (base cfe8a0aea69a4be1b2cd49f9d1f03798cd313bfa, head 388ca9f984bc1559eb21839ba276fea46e891ae4, merge a4d0b4700f05ca7a598b3446d59a8f53fbdd299a)
- Native review: model gpt-6.1-sol/uos/ultra, thread `01a0fc94-6b7b-7cd2-b401-22d17d171503`, turn `01a0fc94-6ff9-75d0-b91c-5e226fb1d946`, exitedReviewMode with turn status `completed`
- Original native severity: P2
- Static validation only: no test, render, inference, or production action was executed while validating.

I_kwDOK6Xdq87x93vR.title: Fix /help flow: do not emit agent-rejected message for bot user
I_kwDOK6Xdq87x93vR.body:
## Summary
When running `/help`, kernel posts the help response but also emits:

`agent rejected: Only human users can invoke the agent (got user.type=Bot)`

This appears to be one symptom of a broader routing problem: bot-authored comments are being treated as valid triggers for bot and agent workflows. As a result, bots can end up conversing with themselves or each other, then emitting rejection noise because only humans may invoke the agent.

A concrete example of the broader failure is the bot-to-bot thread on:
https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-conversation-rewards/issues/340

## Current behavior
- `/help` succeeds (help content is posted).
- Kernel also posts an unrelated agent rejection message for bot user type.
- Bot-authored comments and mentions can trigger downstream bot or agent handling.
- This creates self-replies or bot-to-bot reply chains and repeated `Only human users can invoke the agent` noise.

## Expected behavior
- `/help` should complete without agent-gating rejection noise.
- Agent human-user restriction should only apply to true agent invocation paths, not help command handling.
- Bot-authored comments must not trigger other bots.
- Mentions or commands emitted by bots must be ignored as invocation sources for downstream bot and agent workflows.

## Acceptance criteria
- Triggering `/help` produces only help output.
- No `Only human users can invoke the agent` message appears for `/help`.
- Comments authored by `user.type=Bot` are ignored by agent-invocation routing.
- Bot-authored comments do not trigger other bots or downstream agent workflows.
- No bot-to-bot reply chains occur from bot-emitted mentions or commands.
- Agent restriction behavior remains intact for true human-triggered agent invocation paths.

Relates to ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-kernel#320

I_kwDOMhAZP87FNHmS.title: CowSwap Integration
I_kwDOMhAZP87FNHmS.body:
The users should be able to "deposit anything" and "withdraw anything" basically abstract the assets by natively incorporating CowSwap into the deposit and withdraw transactions on the UI. [^01^]

Deposit flow should allow them to select any asset, and then it should swap and send to our deposit contract. The deposit contract should then return UUSD tokens. This may have a minor conflict with #25 as it has an integration with a direct curve swap (the primary UUSD market.)

The reverse flow should also work, where the user can withdraw into any asset. Again, careful of the existing curve swap code.

---

I assume the best UX is to "lock" or disable the UI elements mid transaction.
1. the user invokes the flow by "depositing ETH"
2. the UI has a notice explaining the current step in the flow, that the user is swapping ETH for LUSD and locks the UI elements so they don't stop mid flow
3. [via a post hook](https://docs.cow.fi/cow-protocol/concepts/order-types/cow-hooks) the swap completes and then the user receives their UUSD.

---

This project requires changes to the UI and creating a CowSwap post hook smart contract.
